title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of Breville and its controlled entities, as well as any contractors or consultants whose terms of engagement apply Breville policies to them. The insider trading prohibition, the section 5.1 ban on limiting economic risk and the section 5.2 short-term trading ban apply to this whole tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Employees likely to have regular access to Inside Information: Breville's Directors, Chief Executive Officer, Group Executives and their senior direct reports, Company Secretaries, Group financial reporting personnel, and any other Employee designated by a Company Secretary from time to time. Closed Periods, the universal approval-to-deal requirement, the short selling and securities lending bans and the margin lending approval attach to this tier.

tiers.name: Closely Connected Parties
tiers.description: Certain family members of a Restricted Person, such as their spouse and dependent children, and any entity which the Restricted Person or such a family member controls or has an ability to control. Restricted Persons must ensure their Closely Connected Parties do not breach the policy.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair, a Restricted Person, whose own requests to deal and exceptional-circumstances applications are approved by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Breville Director (excluding Chair of the Board)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair; requests to deal are approved by the Chair of the Board, and dealings must be notified to a Company Secretary within one business day for ASX disclosure.

tiers.name: Chief Executive Officer, Group Executive, or a Company Secretary
tiers.description: The CEO, direct reports of the CEO, and Company Secretaries; requests to deal are approved by the Chair of the Board. As KMP they must also notify a Company Secretary of any dealing within one business day.

tiers.name: All other Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Senior direct reports of Group Executives, Group financial reporting personnel and other designated Employees; requests to deal are approved by a Company Secretary.

definitions.hedging_definition: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme (including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products) whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant made by Breville to the Employee, irrespective of the outcome under that incentive award or grant. 'Derivative includes a derivative within the meaning of section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as an option, forward contract, swap, future, warrant, cap and collar) and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.'

windows.start_anchor: close of trade on the ASX on 31 December of each year (or, if 31 December is not a Trading Day, the preceding Trading Day)
windows.end_anchor: trading on the ASX opens on the Trading Day following the release of Breville's half-year results

windows.start_anchor: close of trade on the ASX on 30 June of each year (or, if 30 June is not a Trading Day, the preceding Trading Day)
windows.end_anchor: trading on the ASX opens on the Trading Day following the release of Breville's full-year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Breville Board may specify any other period as a Closed Period from time to time (section 4.2(c)). The policy does not say whether such a period or its reasons are confidential, but a refusal of a request to deal is final, unreasoned and must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: Section 5.1 bans any agreement, arrangement or scheme including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products that changes the Employee's economic benefit or risk in Breville shares or an equity incentive award. The defined term Derivative expressly names 'cap and collar' among section 761D derivatives, and there is no venue limitation, so both exchange-traded and OTC puts and calls over Breville shares are caught. The ban applies to every Employee, not just Restricted Persons, and has no approval route.
rules.evidence: Derivative includes a derivative within the meaning of section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as an option, forward contract, swap, future, warrant, cap and collar) and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.

rules.detail: The prohibition is not confined to plan securities: it reaches 'any holding of Breville shares'. There is no carve-out for vested, unrestricted shares and no approval, waiver or exemption route; the section 4.4 exceptional circumstances mechanism relieves only the Closed Period restriction, not section 5.1.
rules.evidence: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme (including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products) whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant made by Breville to the Employee

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested equity-based incentive awards or grants is prohibited, and the closing words make clear this holds whether or not the award ultimately vests.
rules.evidence: in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant made by Breville to the Employee, irrespective of the outcome under that incentive award or grant.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named as such, but a prepaid variable forward, a share swap or an exchangeable is a forward contract or swap within the defined term Derivative and, being an arrangement that changes the Employee's economic benefit or risk in Breville shares, is banned by section 5.1. The words 'any agreement, arrangement or scheme' and 'any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk' give the clause a substance-over-form reach.
rules.evidence: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme (including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products) whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares

rules.detail: Absolute prohibition at any time, with no approval or exceptional circumstances route. Section 4.7 is directed to Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties; the summary in section 9 also lists short selling as a Restricted Persons-only item.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties are prohibited from short selling Breville Securities at any time.

rules.detail: An unusually wide ban: lending Breville Securities to any other party for securities lending or for any other purpose is prohibited outright, not merely lending that facilitates short selling. This bites on any collar or financing structure that contemplates the bank on-lending or rehypothecating the collateral shares.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties are also prohibited from “lending” their Breville Securities to any other party for the purposes of short selling, Securities lending or for any other purpose.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are not named but are section 761D derivatives and transactions in a financial product that alter the economic risk of holding Breville shares, so they fall within the section 5.1 ban; a short CFD would additionally offend the section 4.7 short selling prohibition for Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.

rules.detail: Including Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement is permitted with the prior approval of the Chair, sought through the section 4.3 Request to Deal Form process. Approval may be refused or conditioned without reasons and may be revoked. Involuntary disposals by an approved margin lender exercising its rights are excluded dealings under section 6(e).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair using the approval procedures described in section 4.3 above.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge is not named in the policy and is not within the Dealing definition. An encumbrance granted as part of a loan facility is caught only because the shares are thereby included in a 'similar funding arrangement' under section 4.6, requiring the Chair's approval. A charge unconnected with any funding arrangement is not addressed.
rules.evidence: may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair

rules.detail: There is no general ban on secured financing. The words 'or similar funding arrangement' extend section 4.6 beyond margin loans to a bespoke loan secured on Breville shares, so the funding leg of a collar would be approvable by the Chair even though the derivative legs are not. Nothing distinguishes vested from unvested shares as collateral.
rules.evidence: may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair using the approval procedures described in section 4.3 above.

rules.detail: A three-month buy-and-sell window test applying to all Employees, expressly extended to 'other short-term dealings such as forward contracts', which sweeps in short-dated derivative structures independently of section 5.1.
rules.evidence: No Employee may deal in Breville Securities on a short-term basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period or entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts.

clearance.evidence: The approver may refuse a request, impose conditions on a proposed dealing or revoke a previously granted request, and in each case is not obliged to provide reasons for their action. Any refusal to approve a request will be final and binding, and the person seeking approval must keep that decision confidential.

clearance.tier: Breville Director (excluding Chair of the Board)
clearance.approver: Chair of the Board (application submitted to a Company Secretary on a 'Request to Deal Form')
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within one (1) business day of any dealing
clearance.evidence: Any approval will be provided in writing (which may include by email) and will be valid for a period of 5 business days from (and including) the date of approval. If the approved dealing does not occur in this time, the approval will lapse, and a new request will need to be submitted.

clearance.tier: Chief Executive Officer, Group Executive, or a Company Secretary
clearance.approver: Chair of the Board (application submitted to a Company Secretary on a 'Request to Deal Form')
clearance.post_trade_to: a Company Secretary in writing, where the person is KMP
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within one (1) business day of any dealing
clearance.evidence: To assist Breville to comply with these requirements, Directors and KMP must notify a Company Secretary in writing within one (1) business day of any dealing.
Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties require approval to deal in Breville’s Securities at any time, even outside a Closed Period.

short_term.basis: buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period
carve_outs: acquisition under an offer or invitation made to all or most shareholders, such as a rights issue, share purchase plan, bonus issue or dividend reinvestment plan
disposal through acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back
acquisition under an employee or director equity plan, including on exercise of an option or performance right (subsequent disposal is not carved out)
indirect and incidental trading through a third party managed investment vehicle
involuntary disposal resulting from an approved margin lender or financier exercising its rights
short_term.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period or entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts.

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee), on a 'Request to Deal in Exceptional Circumstances Form'
exceptions.evidence: the person is suffering severe and unforeseen financial hardship;

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee)
exceptions.evidence: the person is bound by a court order, enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement to transfer or sell Breville Securities;

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee)
exceptions.evidence: the person’s circumstances are otherwise exceptional and the proposed dealing is the only reasonable course of action available.
the acquisition of Breville Securities under an offer or invitation made to all or most shareholders, such as a rights issue, share purchase plan, bonus issue or dividend reinvestment plan;
the disposal of Breville Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;

the acquisition of Breville Securities under an employee or director equity plan. This includes where Breville Securities are acquired through the exercise of an option or performance right granted under such a plan (noting, however, that any subsequent disposal of such Securities would be subject to this policy);

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of dealing in Breville Securities by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund, or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that holds Breville Securities as part of its portfolio; and

an involuntary disposal of Breville Securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement (provided the arrangement was previously approved in accordance with this policy).

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties; at inception, before including Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement; to the Chair, via a Request to Deal Form submitted to a Company Secretary; prior approval required before the arrangement is entered into.
Directors and KMP; on any dealing; to a Company Secretary in writing; within one business day.

exemption_authority: Section 4.4 only: the Chair of the Board (or, for the Chair, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee) may approve dealing during a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances (severe and unforeseen financial hardship, legal compulsion, or otherwise exceptional circumstances where the dealing is the only reasonable course of action), for 5 business days and only if the person is not in possession of Inside Information. There is no authority anywhere in the policy to waive the section 5.1 ban on limiting economic risk, the section 4.7 short selling and lending bans, or the section 5.2 short-term trading ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: collar named in the derivative definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivative includes a derivative within the meaning of section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as an option, forward contract, swap, future, warrant, cap and collar) and any other transaction in a financial product that limits the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names a collar as a Derivative product, so the derivative legs of a funded collar fall squarely within the section 5.1 prohibition and cannot be argued outside it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban reaches all shares and all staff
bespoke_clauses.clause: No Employee may enter into any agreement, arrangement or scheme ... whereby the Employee changes the economic benefit or risk derived by the Employee in relation to any holding of Breville shares or an equity-based incentive award or grant ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to plan or unvested securities and applies to every director, employee, contractor and consultant, so there is no class of shares or class of person over whom a collar could be written.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no waiver of the hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 4.4 permits approval to deal during a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances; it relieves only the Closed Period restriction and no provision permits a waiver of section 5.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even severe financial hardship or a court order gives no route to a permitted collar; the only relief available goes to timing, not to the prohibited structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties may not include their Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement without first seeking the approval of the Chair using the approval procedures described in section 4.3 above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on Breville shares is permitted with the Chair's approval, so the funding leg is available in isolation even though the protective legs of a collar are not.

bespoke_clauses.topic: approved lender enforcement is an excluded dealing
bespoke_clauses.clause: an involuntary disposal of Breville Securities that results from a margin lender or financier exercising its rights under a margin lending arrangement (provided the arrangement was previously approved in accordance with this policy).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually protective: a bank enforcing over collateral, including during a Closed Period, does not breach the policy so long as the facility was approved up front, which makes a plain secured loan workable.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no rehypothecation or lending of collateral
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons and their Closely Connected Parties are also prohibited from “lending” their Breville Securities to any other party for the purposes of short selling, Securities lending or for any other purpose.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any structure in which the bank borrows or rehypothecates the pledged shares to hedge its own position is prohibited, so collateral must be held on a no-reuse basis.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forward contracts caught by the short-term rule
bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3-month period or entering into other short-term dealings such as forward contracts.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A forward or short-dated derivative is independently prohibited as short-term dealing, so tenor cannot be used to cure the section 5.1 problem.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver may refuse a request, impose conditions on a proposed dealing or revoke a previously granted request, and in each case is not obliged to provide reasons for their action. Any refusal to approve a request will be final and binding, and the person seeking approval must keep that decision confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the financing leg can be revoked or conditioned without reasons and lapses after 5 business days, so the bank should not treat an approval as a durable condition precedent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closely Connected Parties includes: certain family members of a Restricted Person, such as their spouse and dependent children; and any entity which the Restricted Person or a person referred to in (a) above controls or has an ability to control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing a collar through a spouse or a controlled trust or company does not avoid the prohibitions, and section 5.1 in any event binds the Employee personally.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Breville director or executive. Section 5.1 prohibits every Employee from entering into any agreement, arrangement or scheme, including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products, that changes their economic benefit or risk in any holding of Breville shares or in an equity incentive award, and the defined term Derivative expressly names 'cap and collar'; the ban covers vested and unvested holdings alike, applies to all staff rather than only Restricted Persons, and has no approval, waiver or exceptional-circumstances route. Short-dated structures are separately barred by the section 5.2 three-month short-term trading rule, which names forward contracts, and Restricted Persons may not lend their Breville Securities to any party for any purpose, which blocks rehypothecation of collateral. Only the funding leg is available: including Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement requires the Chair's prior approval under section 4.6, and an involuntary disposal by an approved financier exercising its rights is an excluded dealing under section 6(e), even in a Closed Period. A bank could therefore offer an approved secured loan against Breville shares, but not the put and call legs that would make it a collar.
